sections.h2: West Linn terrain and what buyers check
sections.html:
West Linn occupies the bluffs between the Willamette and Tualatin rivers in Clackamas County, directly across the Willamette from Oregon City. Elevation is about 679 feet, and 0.68 of the city's 8.11 square miles is water. Mary S. Young State Recreation Area and the 26-acre Camassia Natural Area give the city plenty of green space.

For a seller, slope and water are practical matters. The city's planning page links a Water Resource Area Map, a Title 13 Habitat Conservation Area map, a flood plain approval application and a Natural Hazards Mitigation Plan. If your lot is wooded, steep or near a creek, those maps show what a buyer's inspector may ask about.

The city recognizes ten neighborhood associations under Chapter 2 of the municipal code, and its older areas began as separate townsites. An association's boundaries can take in more than one homeowners association, so a seller may deal with both.

  • Willamette. A former townsite that incorporated separately in 1908. The city also lists a Willamette Historic District, where Historic Design Review applies to landmarks and the district.
  • Bolton, Sunset and Multnomah City. Former townsites and developments that later joined the city.
  • Cedaroak, Marylhurst and Hidden Springs. Areas added through annexation.
  • Tanner Basin and Tannler. Infill areas created later.

Older neighborhoods often have larger trees, steeper driveways and homes from several eras on one street. Newer subdivisions carry HOA rules, so a resale certificate or rules packet may be part of the sale.

Historic Design Review applies to a house that is a landmark or sits in the Willamette Historic District. A buyer who wants to change the exterior will ask about it, so find out early. The city planning office can be reached at 503-656-3535.

Higher values raise the bar for condition. Buyers shopping at these price levels often expect updated kitchens and systems, so a house that needs work can sit longer on the market. Many owners have lived in their homes a long time, and some now face a choice about repairs or a move.

Annual precipitation is 44.37 inches, with January the wettest month at 6.78 inches. Moss on roofs, damp crawl spaces, clogged gutters and drainage on sloped lots all show up in inspection reports. Fixing them before listing can cost money and time, which is one reason owners with older houses consider selling as-is.

Clackamas County bills West Linn property owners. Under Measure 50, assessed value growth is capped at 3% a year unless the property changes, which is why the average single-family home has a taxable value of $370,342 against a real market value of $691,382.

Dates to mark:

  • November 16, 2026: full payment for a 3% discount, or two-thirds for 2%.
  • February 16, 2027: second installment under the three-payment plan.
  • May 17, 2027: final installment.
  • December 31, 2026: last day to file a value appeal with the Property Value Appeals Board.

Yellow on the statement means your lender requested payment information and may be paying the tax for you. The county's Assessment and Taxation office takes questions at 503-655-8671, and appeal forms go to the County Clerk at 503-655-8662.

A lien attaches to the property every July 1, so the fall bill already covers a fiscal year that began before most buyers closed. After a July 1 ownership change, the fall statement may leave out the new owner. No statement by November 1? Contact the tax collector for the amount.

State rules put late interest at 1.333% a month, beginning December 16 for the first installment. The title company usually pays or prorates the tax at closing. If you are behind, get a payoff figure before accepting an offer.

Cash gives up a possibly higher list price in return for speed and fewer steps. Listing a West Linn house usually means preparing it, staging, showings, buyer financing and appraisal, and possible repair requests after inspection. A direct cash buyer purchases the house in its current state, and the title company closes it.

Weigh the two on what you would net, not just the headline price. Count repairs, agent fees, months of tax, insurance and utilities, and any HOA dues while the house waits for a buyer.

1. Share the address, condition and your timeline.
  2. Review the written offer, including who pays closing costs.
  3. Escrow opens at a title company, which searches for liens and unpaid taxes.
  4. You sign, the deed is recorded and you receive your proceeds.

If an HOA governs the house, ask for the rules packet or resale certificate early so it is ready when escrow opens.

Nearly all of West Linn is in the West Linn-Wilsonville School District. West Linn High School, Athey Creek and Rosemont Ridge middle schools and four primary schools serve the city. Check your address with the district for the school your children would attend.

sections.h2: Preparing a wooded or sloped lot
sections.html: Trees, hillsides and creeks add charm and questions in equal measure. Before you list, clear gutters and downspouts, check that water runs away from the foundation, and look for soft spots or moss on the roof. If your lot sits near a mapped habitat or water resource area, have the city's map ready so you can answer a buyer on the spot. A short written note about how the yard drains in a heavy January storm will do more for a nervous buyer than any reassurance.

sections.h2: Selling a house you have owned for decades
sections.html: Long-time owners often hold houses that have not been remodeled in years. If that is you, compare three numbers: what an agent thinks the house would bring after updates, what it would cost to do those updates, and what a cash buyer offers for the house as it stands. Then add the months of taxes, insurance and utilities you would carry while waiting. Sometimes the as-is figure comes out closer to the listing figure than you expect, and sometimes it does not. Either way, you decide with real numbers.

sections.h2: Documents to bring to the title office
sections.html:
• Photo ID that matches the deed.
  • Your latest tax statement.
  • Lender name and loan number for any payoff.
  • HOA rules packet or resale certificate, where one applies.
  • Papers for permits, roof work or drainage repairs.

Missing documents cause most small delays, so gather them while offers are still coming in.

faqs.q: Is West Linn in Clackamas County?
faqs.a: Yes. The county assessor and tax collector handle its property tax, and the city sits across the Willamette River from Oregon City.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in West Linn?
faqs.a: $770,200 for owner-occupied homes, based on 2020 to 2024 estimates. It is a citywide number and does not value any single property.

faqs.q: When are Clackamas County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The current-year dates are November 16, 2026, February 16, 2027 and May 17, 2027. Paying in full on the first date earns a 3% discount.

faqs.q: Which school district covers West Linn?
faqs.a: Nearly all of the city is in the West Linn-Wilsonville School District. Its schools include West Linn High School, Athey Creek and Rosemont Ridge middle schools and four primary schools in the city.

faqs.q: Do historic rules apply to my West Linn house?
faqs.a: They can if the house is a historic landmark or in the Willamette Historic District, where Historic Design Review applies. Ask the city planning office at 503-656-3535.
